newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut market mixed on lower turnover.
newsitem.headline: Beirut market mixed on lower turnover.

text.p: Solidere B were the only shares to rise on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Thursday, for the second successive day, while two shares fell, three were unchanged and there was no change in three others.
The LIBX bank index fell 0.53 percent to 153.39. The LISPI and the BLOM general indices fell 0.26 percent to 89.55 and 0.88 percent to 938.15 respectively.
Market turnover fell to 192,557 shares for a value of $1,798,216 from 229,392 shares worth $1,819,211 on Wednesday.
Solidere B rose to $11 from $10.875 amid heavy demand.
"Buyers were obliged to increase prices for the B shares because of a shortage of supply," a broker who asked not to be identified told Reuters.
Solidere A fell to $10.5 from $10.75 amid heavy demand.
"A huge demand for A shares at low to medium prices dragged the shares down a little bit. If demand continues like that then prices will be better," the broker said.
Bank of Beirut fell for the second successive day to $3.875 from $3.9375. Brokers said the drop was a continuing adjustment after this week's sudden rise to $4.
The two other bank shares, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce and Banque Audi, were unchanged at alltime highs of $18.25 and $23.125 respectively.
Of the four industrial firms, Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.28125.
There was no trade in Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
